behaviors.description: Authorized ordinary-user system install resolves the runtime dependency and is readable by a second user.
behaviors.preconditions: Selected target's system helper, real polkit, two distinct ordinary users, fresh named installation and independently prepared A repository; umask 0022.
behaviors.expected: A single app install request deploys exactly the expected app and runtime commits, queried by both users; default and per-user remote sets remain unchanged.

behaviors.description: Authorized ordinary-user update selects advertised B while retaining the runtime.
behaviors.preconditions: A and runtime installed through the system helper, then the remote is pointed to independently prepared B.
behaviors.expected: Update with commit NULL deploys B and retains the runtime commit, visible to both users.

behaviors.description: Authorized ordinary-user uninstall removes the system app for both users.
behaviors.preconditions: Exact app A and runtime commits installed through the selected system helper.
behaviors.expected: Both users receive public NOT_INSTALLED for the removed app, while exact enumeration and queries retain only the runtime.

behaviors.description: Named system remote addition, URL modification and removal persist across users.
behaviors.preconditions: Two real user identities and fresh named installation; default and per-user remote snapshots recorded.
behaviors.expected: The reader observes A and then B URLs from fresh library objects, then no remote after removal. Both users' default/per-user snapshots remain unchanged.

behaviors.description: Installation no-interaction suppresses real polkit requests while preserving authorization failure.
behaviors.preconditions: Reader requires authentication; independent process-scoped recording agent rejects every request; system languages seeded to de.
behaviors.expected: Interactive/silent/interactive config attempts all fail with public permission-denied. Interactive attempts reach the agent; silent does not. Getter reflects setter, languages stay de and installed commits remain unchanged.

behaviors.description: Transactions inherit and override no-interaction with observable polkit request suppression.
behaviors.preconditions: Reader requires authentication to uninstall seeded A; independent recording agent rejects all requests.
behaviors.expected: New transaction getters inherit both installation settings and reflect overrides in both directions. Interactive modes reach the agent, silent modes do not; all uninstall attempts fail permission-denied and preserve exact app/runtime commits.

mappings.rationale: A real authorized non-root transaction installs app and implicit runtime; fresh public queries and exact enumerations by two distinct users match independent commits.
After A is visible to both users, authorized update with commit NULL selects advertised B. Both users observe B and the unchanged runtime.
Real authorized uninstall is followed by public NOT_INSTALLED errors for both users and exact runtime-only enumeration.
The reader reopens the named installation after addition and URL modification, then both users enumerate no remotes after removal. Default and per-user remote snapshots stay unchanged.

A process-scoped agent records actual polkit requests in both interactive controls and none for no-interaction. Every rejected configuration operation returns public permission-denied, getters match and state remains unchanged.

Getter checks cover inheritance and explicit overrides in both directions, and a rejecting real polkit agent distinguishes interactive and silent transactions. All denied uninstalls preserve both users' exact installed refs/commits.

notes: Authorization failures accept the public D-Bus AccessDenied or Flatpak permission-denied error. An aborted transaction must expose a permission-denied underlying operation error for the requested ref; an unrelated failure cannot satisfy the assertion.

Execution requires explicit BLACKBOX_SYSTEM_TEST_ROOT provisioning, with the helper and library from the selected target build. Root only orchestrates disposable state and switches users; every target library operation executes with the asserted ordinary UID.

The recording agent registers for the exact client process, never authenticates, and dies with its parent. No root-user-namespace or property-only assertion substitutes for real authorization behavior.
Nested command records, stdout, stderr and statuses remain in evidence. Actual client API-call traces are forwarded for library coverage verification.
